Hi Rosangela,

Thank you for asking. This error is because your shapefile and image do not have the same projection. 

Projection is important when you are trying to overlay images or trying to use the same shapefile for different orthomosaics (e.g., different flights on the same field trial). 

If you are using images from Lab (e.g., seeds, leaves, etc.) you can ignore the projection to extract data using fieldInfo().

In this case, the solution is to use projection=FALSE on fieldInfo().

EX1.Info<- fieldInfo(mosaic = EX1.Indices[[c("NGRDI","BGI","myIndex")]],
                     fieldShape = EX1.Shape$fieldShape,
                     buffer = 0.05,

n.core = 3,
                     projection=F)

Please, let me know if it workes.

All the best,
Filipe

Hi there,

The script below seems that is working well for your image. Please, let me know if you have questions. Just one point for your attention, your mosaic (Foto.tif) still on Digital Numbers (normally with pixels' values varying from 0 to 250). Before starting any analysis or extracting data, it's important to make the radiometric calibration first to get radiance and/or reflectance (biological meaning).

#################
### FIELDimageR ###
#################

library(FIELDimageR)
library(raster)
EX1 <- stack("Foto.tif")
plotRGB(EX1)



EX1.RemSoil<-fieldMask(EX1)



EX1.Shape<-fieldShape(mosaic = EX1.RemSoil$newMosaic,ncols = 20, nrows = 50)


# Attention: Pixel values are Digital Numbers (DN) - Layers Red, Green, and Blue (from 0 to 250)
EX1.Indices<- fieldIndex(mosaic = EX1.RemSoil$newMosaic,  
                         index = c("NGRDI","BGI"), 
                         myIndex = c("(Red-Blue)/Green"))


plotRGB(EX1.Indices)
plot(EX1.Shape$fieldShape, add=T)

EX1.Info<- fieldInfo(mosaic = EX1.Indices[[c("NGRDI","BGI","myIndex")]],
                     fieldShape = EX1.Shape$fieldShape,
                     buffer = 0.05,
                     n.core = 3,
                     projection=F)

EX1.Info$plotValue



Hope this can help you...!!!

All the best,
Filipe

Hi Kassim,

Thank you for asking. The pixel values output from cameras/sensors normally is on Digital Numbers (8 bits channel normally are from 0 to 250). The most common analysis pathway is to transform DN to radiance by using the camera/sensor setups. For this, you need to check the manual of your platform and/or Google about the transformation equations for each band/wavelength/layer. Another solution is to contact directly the company that provided your sensor and asks for the formulas/equations. 

Normally for biological research, radiance values are transformed to reflectance values to compare experiments/genotypes. Reflectance is the ratio between the incidence radiance (e.g, from the Sun) compared to the radiance reflected from the surface (e.g., plants). The variation of reflectance observed among genotypes is used to evaluate/correlate with biomass, maturity, tolerance, resistance, yield, etc. To transform radiance to reflectance you can (1) have a reflectance sensor directly connected to your Phenotyping Platform (e.g., connected to the drone) or (2) the most common is to use a reflectance panel in the field on the same day and time that you collect the data/images. These panels have some materials with known reflectance (e.g., 40%, 60%, etc.) that are used to correct pixels values. 

You can read more about other methods in this paper: https://doi.org/10.3390/rs11161917

Hope this can help you.

All the best,
Filipe

On Sat, Mar 6, 2021 at 6:10 PM fmatias <filipem...@gmail.com> wrote:

Hi Kassim,

Thank you for asking. The pixel values output from cameras/sensors normally is on Digital Numbers (8 bits channel normally are from 0 to 250). The most common analysis pathway is to transform DN to radiance by using the camera/sensor setups. For this, you need to check the manual of your platform and/or Google about the transformation equations for each band/wavelength/layer. Another solution is to contact directly the company that provided your sensor and asks for the formulas/equations. 

Normally for biological research, radiance values are transformed to reflectance values to compare experiments/genotypes. Reflectance is the ratio between the incidence radiance (e.g, from the Sun) compared to the radiance reflected from the surface (e.g., plants). The variation of reflectance observed among genotypes is used to evaluate/correlate with biomass, maturity, tolerance, resistance, yield, etc. To transform radiance to reflectance you can (1) have a reflectance sensor directly connected to your Phenotyping Platform (e.g., connected to the drone) or (2) the most common is to use a reflectance panel in the field on the same day and time that you collect the data/images. These panels have some materials with known reflectance (e.g., 40%, 60%, etc.) that are used to correct pixels values. 

You can read more about other methods in this paper: https://doi.org/10.3390/rs11161917

Hope this can help you.

All the best,
Filipe

Hi there,

The script below seems that is working well for your image. Please, let me know if you have questions. Just one point for your attention, your mosaic (Foto.tif) still on Digital Numbers (normally with pixels' values varying from 0 to 250). Before starting any analysis or extracting data, it's important to make the radiometric calibration first to get radiance and/or reflectance (biological meaning).

#################
### FIELDimageR ###
#################

library(FIELDimageR)
library(raster)
EX1 <- stack("Foto.tif")
plotRGB(EX1)



EX1.RemSoil<-fieldMask(EX1)



EX1.Shape<-fieldShape(mosaic = EX1.RemSoil$newMosaic,ncols = 20, nrows = 50)


# Attention: Pixel values are Digital Numbers (DN) - Layers Red, Green, and Blue (from 0 to 250)
EX1.Indices<- fieldIndex(mosaic = EX1.RemSoil$newMosaic,  
                         index = c("NGRDI","BGI"), 
                         myIndex = c("(Red-Blue)/Green"))


plotRGB(EX1.Indices)
plot(EX1.Shape$fieldShape, add=T)


EX1.Info<- fieldInfo(mosaic = EX1.Indices[[c("NGRDI","BGI","myIndex")]],
                     fieldShape = EX1.Shape$fieldShape,
                     buffer = 0.05,
                     n.core = 3,
                     projection=F)

EX1.Info$plotValue



Hope this can help you...!!!

All the best,
Filipe

Hi Rosangela,

Thank you for asking. This error is because your shapefile and image do not have the same projection. 

Projection is important when you are trying to overlay images or trying to use the same shapefile for different orthomosaics (e.g., different flights on the same field trial). 

If you are using images from Lab (e.g., seeds, leaves, etc.) you can ignore the projection to extract data using fieldInfo().

In this case, the solution is to use projection=FALSE on fieldInfo().

EX1.Info<- fieldInfo(mosaic = EX1.Indices[[c("NGRDI","BGI","myIndex")]],
                     fieldShape = EX1.Shape$fieldShape,
                     buffer = 0.05,
                     n.core = 3,
                     projection=F)

Please, let me know if it workes.

All the best,
Filipe

On Sat, Mar 6, 2021 at 6:10 PM fmatias <filipem...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi Kassim,

Thank you for asking. The pixel values output from cameras/sensors normally is on Digital Numbers (8 bits channel normally are from 0 to 250). The most common analysis pathway is to transform DN to radiance by using the camera/sensor setups. For this, you need to check the manual of your platform and/or Google about the transformation equations for each band/wavelength/layer. Another solution is to contact directly the company that provided your sensor and asks for the formulas/equations. 

Normally for biological research, radiance values are transformed to reflectance values to compare experiments/genotypes. Reflectance is the ratio between the incidence radiance (e.g, from the Sun) compared to the radiance reflected from the surface (e.g., plants). The variation of reflectance observed among genotypes is used to evaluate/correlate with biomass, maturity, tolerance, resistance, yield, etc. To transform radiance to reflectance you can (1) have a reflectance sensor directly connected to your Phenotyping Platform (e.g., connected to the drone) or (2) the most common is to use a reflectance panel in the field on the same day and time that you collect the data/images. These panels have some materials with known reflectance (e.g., 40%, 60%, etc.) that are used to correct pixels values. 

You can read more about other methods in this paper: https://doi.org/10.3390/rs11161917

Hope this can help you.

All the best,
Filipe
